# bugs #4070: sdas8051 assembles the address of the fourth byte of an __sfr32 as 0xFF

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4070/
- Category: [Analyzed, not fixed](../../unresolved.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17158
- Recommended action: Choose between the valmasks patch in the ticket and the upstream asxxxx design. Add a test that reads each byte through an __sfr.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

With sdcc r17158 for mcs51, an assignment of 0 to `__sfr32 __at(0xa3a5a6a7)` writes the SFRs 0xa7,
0xa6, 0xa5, and 0xff. The listing shows `F5 A7`, `F5 A6`, `F5 A5`, and `F5 FF` for the four `mov`
instructions, and the last one must be `F5 A3`.

## Known

sdcc emits the operand of the fourth instruction as `(_X >> 24) & 0xFF`. `rngchk` in
`sdas/asxxsrc/asexpr.c` sign-extends every expression value from the width that `exprmasks` sets,
and `sdas/as8051/i51mch.c` calls `exprmasks(3)`. Bits 24 to 31 of the symbol value are therefore
copies of bit 23 when the shift is applied. The byte is 0xFF for the address list in the ticket.
By the code it is 0x00 for an address list with bit 23 clear, which was not assembled.

`exprmasks` sets `a_bytes` together with the masks. `a_bytes` is also the number of address bytes
that `outrb` in `sdas/asxxsrc/asout.c` writes to the T line of a one-byte relocation. In the
seventh comment a maintainer reports that `exprmasks(4)` corrects the byte and breaks relocation
in the linker. That was not tried here.

The patch attached to the tenth comment gives the arithmetic its own width through a new function
`valmasks` and leaves `a_bytes` at 3. It was not applied or tested here. In the last comment a
maintainer prefers the design of upstream asxxxx, which has one width and different relocation
output.

`support/regression/tests/sfr16.c` declares an `__sfr32` and reads and writes it only as a whole.
Both directions use the same wrong address for the fourth byte, so the test does not show the
defect.

## Open

The first decision is between the two designs. For either one, a comparison of the `.rel` and
`.ihx` files of other mcs51 code before and after the change shows whether bytes other than the
`__sfr32` addresses change.

A regression test is needed. The ninth comment proposes one. It declares an `__sfr32` over
registers that ucsim implements and declares the same registers as `__sfr` and `__sfr16`. It
writes through one declaration and reads through the others.
